selection_scope: Nine selected domains with six public question families each; not an exhaustive partition of philosophy.

questions.prompt: Why is there something rather than nothing, and where may explanation lawfully terminate?
questions.native_problem: Ground, sufficient reason and explanatory termination.
questions.native_reference: Leibniz, Principles of Nature and Grace §7; Heidegger, Introduction to Metaphysics.

questions.prompt: How can reality be one while containing genuine plurality?
questions.native_problem: Unity, plurality and dependence without erasure.
questions.native_reference: Plato, Parmenides; Aristotle, Metaphysics.

questions.prompt: What is the relation between repeatable properties and particular things?
questions.native_problem: Realism, nominalism and trope theories of universals.
questions.native_reference: Plato, Republic; Aristotle, Categories and Metaphysics.

questions.prompt: What makes a thing the same thing through change?
questions.native_problem: Numerical identity, continuity, constitution and persistence.
questions.native_reference: Locke, Essay Concerning Human Understanding II.27; Parfit, Reasons and Persons.

questions.prompt: What makes possibility and necessity true?
questions.native_problem: Modal truth, accessibility and possible-world semantics.
questions.native_reference: Kripke, Naming and Necessity; Lewis, On the Plurality of Worlds.

questions.prompt: Is time fundamental, emergent, tenseless or essentially becoming?
questions.native_problem: A-series, B-series, passage and change.
questions.native_reference: Aristotle, Physics IV; McTaggart, The Unreality of Time.

questions.prompt: What warrants belief in a world independent of present experience?
questions.native_problem: External-world skepticism and perceptual warrant.
questions.native_reference: Descartes, Meditations I; Moore, Proof of an External World.

questions.prompt: What warrants projecting observed regularities into unobserved cases?
questions.native_problem: Hume's problem of induction and projectibility.
questions.native_reference: Hume, Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding IV; Goodman, Fact, Fiction, and Forecast.

questions.prompt: Why can justified true belief still fail to be knowledge?
questions.native_problem: Gettier luck and analyses of knowledge.
questions.native_reference: Plato, Theaetetus; Gettier, Is Justified True Belief Knowledge?

questions.prompt: How can knowledge be warranted independently of particular sensory experience?
questions.native_problem: A priori warrant, rational insight and empiricism.
questions.native_reference: Kant, Critique of Pure Reason; BonJour, In Defense of Pure Reason.

questions.prompt: When does another person's word give knowledge rather than merely borrowed belief?
questions.native_problem: Testimonial warrant, reductionism and social dependence.
questions.native_reference: Coady, Testimony; Hume, Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding X.

questions.prompt: How should rational peers revise when evidence underdetermines a shared conclusion?
questions.native_problem: Peer disagreement, conciliation and steadfastness.
questions.native_reference: Feldman and Warfield, Disagreement; Christensen, Epistemology of Disagreement.

questions.prompt: How can a truth-bearing sentence coherently say of itself that it is false?
questions.native_problem: Semantic self-reference, truth predicates and hierarchy.
questions.native_reference: Tarski, The Concept of Truth in Formalized Languages; Kripke, Outline of a Theory of Truth.

questions.prompt: Which comprehension principle fails in Russell's paradox, and what survives?
questions.native_problem: Unrestricted comprehension and axiomatic set formation.
questions.native_reference: Russell, Principles of Mathematics; Zermelo, Investigations in the Foundations of Set Theory I.

questions.prompt: What do incompleteness theorems show—and not show—about formal proof and truth?
questions.native_problem: Formal consistency, completeness and arithmetical truth.
questions.native_reference: Gödel, On Formally Undecidable Propositions (1931).

questions.prompt: How can tiny differences accumulate into an apparently impossible boundary change?
questions.native_problem: Vagueness, tolerance principles and borderline cases.
questions.native_reference: Eubulides' sorites tradition; Williamson, Vagueness.

questions.prompt: How do words refer to things and carry meaning across speakers and contexts?
questions.native_problem: Sense, reference, causal naming and context.
questions.native_reference: Frege, On Sense and Reference; Kripke, Naming and Necessity.

questions.prompt: What makes one continuation an instance of following a rule rather than another?
questions.native_problem: Normativity of meaning and rule-following skepticism.
questions.native_reference: Wittgenstein, Philosophical Investigations; Kripke, Wittgenstein on Rules and Private Language.

questions.prompt: How are mental states related to physical states?
questions.native_problem: Dualism, physicalism, functionalism and realization.
questions.native_reference: Descartes, Meditations VI; Ryle, The Concept of Mind.

questions.prompt: Why and how is physical or functional processing accompanied by experience?
questions.native_problem: Phenomenal consciousness and the explanatory gap.
questions.native_reference: Chalmers, Facing Up to the Problem of Consciousness; Nagel, What Is It Like to Be a Bat?

questions.prompt: How can a present mental state be about something absent, unreal or possible?
questions.native_problem: Aboutness, content and representation.
questions.native_reference: Brentano, Psychology from an Empirical Standpoint; Searle, Intentionality.

questions.prompt: What preserves a person through bodily, psychological and narrative change?
questions.native_problem: Personal identity, continuity, fission and survival.
questions.native_reference: Locke, Essay II.27; Parfit, Reasons and Persons.

questions.prompt: Can an agent be free or responsible in a causally ordered world?
questions.native_problem: Compatibilism, sourcehood, alternatives and determinism.
questions.native_reference: Hume, Enquiry VIII; Frankfurt, Alternate Possibilities and Moral Responsibility.

questions.prompt: What warrants attributing consciousness or agency to another human, animal or AI?
questions.native_problem: Other minds, behavioral evidence and machine mentality.
questions.native_reference: Turing, Computing Machinery and Intelligence; Nagel, What Is It Like to Be a Bat?

questions.prompt: What distinguishes causation from correlation, regularity or description?
questions.native_problem: Counterfactual, interventionist, regularity and process accounts.
questions.native_reference: Hume, Enquiry VII; Pearl, Causality.

questions.prompt: What makes a scientific generalization a law or explanation?
questions.native_problem: Laws, models, explanation and necessity.
questions.native_reference: Hempel and Oppenheim, Studies in the Logic of Explanation; van Fraassen, The Scientific Image.

questions.prompt: When does a higher-level description add genuine novelty rather than convenient compression?
questions.native_problem: Reduction, multiple realization, emergence and universality.
questions.native_reference: Nagel, The Structure of Science; Anderson, More Is Different.

questions.prompt: How do quantum probabilities relate to definite measurement records?
questions.native_problem: Measurement, decoherence, outcomes and interpretation.
questions.native_reference: von Neumann, Mathematical Foundations of Quantum Mechanics; Bell, Against Measurement.

questions.prompt: Which combinations of locality, realism and independence are constrained by Bell-type results?
questions.native_problem: Bell inequalities, locality and hidden-variable assumptions.
questions.native_reference: Bell, On the Einstein Podolsky Rosen Paradox (1964).

questions.prompt: Is probability objective chance, rational credence, frequency or model-relative uncertainty?
questions.native_problem: Interpretations of probability and objective chance.
questions.native_reference: Kolmogorov, Foundations of the Theory of Probability; de Finetti, Theory of Probability.

questions.prompt: What, if anything, can bridge descriptive premises and normative conclusions?
questions.native_problem: Hume's is–ought distinction and bridge principles.
questions.native_reference: Hume, Treatise of Human Nature III.i.1.

questions.prompt: Are moral claims stance-independently true, constructed, plural or systematically mistaken?
questions.native_problem: Moral realism, constructivism, pluralism and error theory.
questions.native_reference: Moore, Principia Ethica; Mackie, Ethics: Inventing Right and Wrong.

questions.prompt: Is the good authoritative because it is commanded, or commanded because it is good?
questions.native_problem: Normative authority and the Euthyphro dilemma.
questions.native_reference: Plato, Euthyphro.

questions.prompt: How should rights, duties and aggregate consequences constrain one another?
questions.native_problem: Deontology, consequentialism, thresholds and trolley cases.
questions.native_reference: Kant, Groundwork; Bentham, Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation.

questions.prompt: How should value across different possible populations be compared without laundering persons?
questions.native_problem: Population ethics, aggregation and the repugnant conclusion.
questions.native_reference: Parfit, Reasons and Persons, Part IV.

questions.prompt: What grounds responsibility, partial duties and permissible sacrifice?
questions.native_problem: Responsibility, reactive attitudes, demandingness and special obligations.
questions.native_reference: Strawson, Freedom and Resentment; Williams, Persons, Character and Morality.

questions.prompt: What makes political or institutional authority legitimate?
questions.native_problem: Consent, authorization, obligation and legitimacy.
questions.native_reference: Hobbes, Leviathan; Locke, Second Treatise of Government.

questions.prompt: How should liberty and equality constrain one another?
questions.native_problem: Negative and positive liberty, equal standing and institutions.
questions.native_reference: Berlin, Two Concepts of Liberty; Rawls, A Theory of Justice.

questions.prompt: Which distributions of resources, capabilities and burdens are just?
questions.native_problem: Equality, entitlement, desert, need and capability.
questions.native_reference: Rawls, A Theory of Justice; Nozick, Anarchy, State, and Utopia.

questions.prompt: How can groups sustain public goods without coercion, free-riding or capture?
questions.native_problem: Collective action, commons and cooperation.
questions.native_reference: Olson, The Logic of Collective Action; Ostrom, Governing the Commons.

questions.prompt: How should power, domination, oppression and extraction be distinguished and resisted?
questions.native_problem: Structural power, exploitation, discipline and domination.
questions.native_reference: Marx, Capital I; Foucault, Discipline and Punish.

questions.prompt: Who may represent future, nonhuman, ecological or incapacitated bearers, and under what limits?
questions.native_problem: Guardianship, proxy standing, future people and ecological representation.
questions.native_reference: Singer, Animal Liberation; Jonas, The Imperative of Responsibility; Stone, Should Trees Have Standing?

questions.prompt: Can genuine values conflict without a single complete ranking?
questions.native_problem: Value pluralism, incommensurability and tragic choice.
questions.native_reference: Berlin, The Crooked Timber of Humanity; Williams, Moral Luck.

questions.prompt: Is beauty objective, relational, culturally constructed or judgment-dependent?
questions.native_problem: Aesthetic judgment, universality and taste.
questions.native_reference: Kant, Critique of Judgment; Hume, Of the Standard of Taste.

questions.prompt: What makes something art, and what constrains interpretation?
questions.native_problem: Artworld, expression, intention and interpretation.
questions.native_reference: Danto, The Artworld; Gadamer, Truth and Method.

questions.prompt: What can make a finite life meaningful?
questions.native_problem: Meaning, purpose, value and finitude.
questions.native_reference: Camus, The Myth of Sisyphus; Nagel, The Absurd.

questions.prompt: How should a worldview account for suffering without explaining it away?
questions.native_problem: Suffering, pessimism, absurdity and practical response.
questions.native_reference: Schopenhauer, The World as Will and Representation; Camus, The Myth of Sisyphus.

questions.prompt: Why is death bad, neutral or transformative for a finite bearer?
questions.native_problem: Deprivation, annihilation, fear and mortality.
questions.native_reference: Epicurus, Letter to Menoeceus; Nagel, Death.

questions.prompt: Does explanation require a necessary being, necessary truth or declared boundary?
questions.native_problem: Cosmological arguments, necessity and regress.
questions.native_reference: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I q.2; Leibniz, Principles of Nature and Grace.

questions.prompt: How can extensive suffering coexist with perfect power, knowledge and goodness?
questions.native_problem: Logical and evidential problems of evil.
questions.native_reference: Lactantius, De Ira Dei; Plantinga, God, Freedom, and Evil.

questions.prompt: Why would a perfectly loving ultimate reality remain nonresistantly hidden?
questions.native_problem: Divine hiddenness and nonbelief.
questions.native_reference: Schellenberg, Divine Hiddenness and Human Reason.

questions.prompt: How should incompatible religious truth claims and convergent practices be compared?
questions.native_problem: Pluralism, exclusivism, inclusivism and translation.
questions.native_reference: Hick, An Interpretation of Religion.

questions.prompt: What epistemic weight can mystical or ineffable experience carry?
questions.native_problem: Mystical experience, ineffability, testimony and interpretation.
questions.native_reference: James, The Varieties of Religious Experience; Stace, Mysticism and Philosophy.

questions.prompt: Can nondual insight dissolve the self-world distinction without erasing finite agency?
questions.native_problem: Nonduality, selfhood, emptiness and liberation.
questions.native_reference: Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad; Śaṅkara, Brahma Sūtra Bhāṣya; Nāgārjuna, Mūlamadhyamakakārikā.
